chapter_seo_title: RMJI Chapter 611: Han Li’s Welcome to the Sect and the Battle Over a Special Constitution
chapter_meta_description: Han Li arrives at the Falling Cloud Sect’s main hall, where elders openly fight over a Metal Forging Constitution disciple. The allocation begins—and he’s sent to Tianquan Peak as an outer disciple.
og_title: Chapter 611: The Steel-Forge Constitution – A Battle Over One Disciple
og_description: Sect elders squabble over a special body type. Han Li watches, learns, and ends up in the quietest corner of the Falling Cloud Sect.
twitter_title: RMJI 611: Don’t be the trophy. Be the one nobody notices.
twitter_description: The sect allocation scene you didn’t know you needed. Corp politics, spiritual root classism, and why Han Li’s mediocrity is a superpower.

lore_anchors.definition: A rare special physique with a natural, high-efficiency affinity for metal-attribute qi. Such disciples are prized by peaks that specialize in metal-element techniques.
A sect member assigned to labor duties (crafting, gathering, guard) with limited cultivation time. They are lower in status than inner disciples but can earn merit for Foundation Establishment Pills.
A full-time cultivation disciple exempted from mundane duties, selected based on spiritual root quality. They represent the sect’s core talent pipeline.
A Xi Kingdom sect with six main peaks. The Sect Leader, Wei Yiming, is a late Foundation Establishment cultivator. The sect practices a hybrid of orthodox and practical cultivation.
A rare, bottleneck-breaking alchemical treasure. Outer disciples must perform extraordinary deeds to earn one, reinforcing the Mortal Stream’s scarcity logic.
One of the Falling Cloud Sect’s six peaks. Its master is described as lenient, and the peak is considered a relatively quiet, low-pressure posting.
A warrior-focused peak within the Falling Cloud Sect, specializing in metal and sword techniques. The elder here argued aggressively for the Metal Forging disciple.
A fire-attribute peak within the sect. Its elder claimed the Metal Forging disciple, arguing that their techniques could still benefit him.
The group of six major mountains that form the core of the Falling Cloud Sect’s territory. The main peak towers at three to four thousand zhang.
An informal term for the internal competition among the six peaks for resources, talent, and cultivation techniques. This rivalry shapes how disciples are divided.

cultural_notes_faq.a: A rare special physique that grants an extremely high natural affinity for metal-attribute qi, making the cultivator far more efficient at learning metal-element techniques.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are the elders fighting over this one disciple?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because a special constitution guarantees faster growth and higher ceiling for their peak, which translates into sect influence, resources, and bragging rights.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why was Han Li sent to Tianquan Peak?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because he has “false spiritual roots”—a common, low-potential set. He was automatically classified as an outer disciple and assigned to whichever peak had space, not because anyone wanted him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is being an outer affairs disciple bad?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s not cruelly punished, but it’s structurally limiting. Han Li must complete labor tasks and can only cultivate in his spare time. Advancement requires rare merit or extreme luck.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Han Li argue or try to get a better placement?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He recognizes that being unnoticed is safer. Attracting attention as a “special talent” invites scrutiny, favors, and enemies—all of which contradict his core survival doctrine.
